week_in_brief: Buyer's market fully here, and marketing budgets finally have somewhere productive to go.

items.headline: Concessions at 46%—but price cuts aren't the story
items.whats_happening: Seller concessions hit 46.2% of home sales this spring—highest rate since 2019—with Sun Belt markets leading at 75% (Nash ville), 71% (Charlotte), 68% (Atlanta), per Redfin. But here's the nuance: these are repairs, closing costs, and rate buydowns, not price cuts. Median price is stable at $425K. Sellers are negotiating terms, not equity.
items.so_what: Stop running price-strength messaging. Concessions are a positioning opportunity—market ads on rate buydowns, closing cost credits, and inspection flexibility. Buyers who left during the hot market are back; they need to hear "leverage" not "appreciation."

items.headline: Entry-level inventory just disappeared
items.whats_happening: Only one in seven new hmes sold for under $300K in May (vs. one in five a year ago), per Inman. Builders can't pencil entry-level hmes at current costs, so they're moving upmarket. First-time buyers are being squeezed out of the new-construction pipeline entirely.
items.so_what: Your first-time buyer volume is shrinking structurally. Shift CAM tiition and marketing spend toward repeat buyers, move-up transactions, and referral systems. The funnel changed—adjust before your competitors do.

items.headline: Proprietary listing platforms are the new moat
items.whats_happening: Hgward Hanna launched HannaList, a pre-MLS listing tool generating 4x more leads than MLS-only exposure, per RISMedia. CEO Hoby Hanna warned that Google and AI portals threaten brokerage control of listing data, and argued that proprietary lead-gen tech is now table stakes. Meanwhile, United Country bundled BullseyeAI—an LLM-powered assistant for CRM, email, and listing gen‑4at no extra cost to 500 affiliates to retain agents worried about tech costs.
items.so_what: If you're relying on Zillow and Realtor.com for listing exposure, you're renting your pipeline. Google's new Search Console AI Performance Reports (announced June 15) let you track AI search visibility alongside traditional organic—meaning you can finally measure whether your site content is being cited in AI Overviews. Invest there. Own the lead source.

items.headline: AI-generated ads now get labeled—and users will notice
items.whats_happening: Meta expanded transparency labels on ads created or edited with generative AI, visible through "About this ad," per Meta Newsroom. The platform can also detect signals from third-party AI tools. Every AI-assisted ad is now subject to user scrutin{. TikTok, meanwhile, expanded Symphony AI to let advertisers turn text/images into platform-native videos at scale—solving content fatigue for multi-location brands.
items.so_what: Transparency is the new trust lever. If you're using AI to scale listing ads or agent recruitment creative, make sure the output is truthful and compliant. And if you're not using AI video tools yet (TikTok Symphony, Runway, Synthesia), your content production is about to look slow and expensive compared to brokerages that are.

this_weeks_take: The market finally shifted. Buyers have leverage, sellers are negotiating, and marketing dollars can actually move deals again. The brokerages winning right now aren't the ones with the most listings—they're the ones who rebuilt their tech stack and repositioned their messaging before everyone else figured it out.
